With that being settled, I have the following goals in mind:
Easy to use and quick to understand
Flexible enough for unique use cases
Advanced customization options via style hooks
All in all, the package should be a well-rounded solution for the typical bachelor’s thesis writing process. Easy for newcomers but powerful for experienced
typesetting users, accessible on the official package registry,
There are two main parts: The package itself and the starter template. Conceptually, the package is the real content with styles and conventions, whereas the
template can be thought of as a new project starter.

By providing a ready to use template with chapters, typical configurations and compilation scripts already set up, users can get going simply by invoking
. This will create a new directory with the template and all necessary files.
We expose all sections as individual functions so users can opt-out of the opinionated default order. Inserting an appendix is as simple as calling
. These functions provide the same customization options as the complete
We also provide different premade thesis styles, controlling the default style for the individual sections, allowing users to quickly switch between completely
different style variants they can build upon later on. This is simply added as another parameter to the
invocation, users can switch between German and English language. Every text content passes
function, returning the appropriate variant from a central translation dictionary based on the current
Style hooks are very powerful and allow users to override stylings as well as the whole content of individual sections. By adhering to the principle of only using
-rules inside the package, users retain the ability to fully override all styling.

, the package browser on the web, is effectively just a mirror of this GitHub repo. Submitting a new package is therefore as simple as opening a
Create a new branch on the locally cloned fork
Create and push a new commit
Open a Pull Request on the upstream packages repo
